note: The piano's moments (his idea, 10-29: "piano solo moment, or some motif that not necessary following the same phrase across the track, as even that gets repetitive"; his ear on the sketches: "color in breakdown - great", "either solo or second riff both sound good"). Two moments, neither a must: a share of the themes where each fits takes it, so it never becomes the next repetition. **The solo:** a long breakdown's last phrase goes to the piano alone, a free line made of the keys' own notes (the phrase's, or the hook's where a hook is the keys, never the hook itself, so its return stays an event) in calls and answers over its own soft chords, then a step back for the section after. It plays at the keys' own level, not in front. **The second riff:** in a long stretch of one hook (a long main or drop), eight bars of the hook's notes over the same chords on a new two-bar rhythm, its top reaching the chord's tones over the hook, then the hook again. Every number is a starting point for listening.

leans.says: the one lean (src/lean.ts) on each moment's chance, about the house's centre: Loom (the form's length and its development) favours both, Spark (a busier, brighter keys part) the riff

solo.says: a breakdown run of `least` bars or more that a stated section follows: its last `bars` go to the piano alone

cells.says: each a two-bar cell of the line: [sixteenth 0-31, beats held, accent, ms late (the rubato), mark]; a mark `s` is a chord tone on a strong place, `p` a passing note by step, `L` a landing (a chord tone held), `C` the cadence's landing on the chord's root with its chord under it

shapes.says: each cell's contour, the line's height across its notes from 0 (the line's floor) to 1 (its ceiling)

riff.says: a main or a drop of `least` bars or more stating one hook: `bars` of it, from a line at least `after` bars in and `before` bars from its end, play the hook's notes on a new rhythm

cell.says: a four-bar cell: [bar, sixteenth, note, beats held, accent]; a note `h<i>` is the hook's i-th note (its order, cycled), `c<k>` the bar's chord's k-th tone over the hook's highest note: a call that rises, an answer home through the hook's own fall
